verdict_reason: Public documentation is available at neo4j.com/docs, and the Aura API uses OAuth 2.0 with credentials creatable by all Aura tiers, paired with a no-credit-card entry point. The API surface spans instance management, Cypher query execution, and GraphQL, giving reasonable breadth. No sales contact, partner approval, or app review is required to obtain developer credentials.
open_questions: Input hint URL https://neo4j.com/docs/api/ returns a 404 'Page not found'; canonical documentation was taken from https://neo4j.com/docs/ instead.
OAuth scopes/permissions documentation was not found in the evidence; the Aura page states credentials inherit user-account roles and capabilities rather than listing scopes.
Core Aura/Neo4j API rate limits were not documented in the supplied sources; the only numeric limits found apply to the separate Neo4j Labs NAMS service.
No evidence of vendor-documented webhooks or event callbacks was present in the supplied sources.
Official SDK language list was not present in the evidence; sources surfaced only a Java Reference page and a general client-libraries pointer.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found in the evidence.
The official Neo4j MCP server is described as a local, downloadable binary rather than a hosted endpoint, so no public hosted MCP URL is documented.
Multiple API surfaces exist (Aura REST/management API, HTTP Query API, GraphQL API); api_type was classified as REST but the evidence is fragmented across pages.
GraphQL API documentation separately mentions API key and JWT authentication, which is not reflected in the Aura API auth methods claim.
